Hmm, but no documented executions, no organised pogroms against trans; courts moving toward decriminalisation. Dossier 4 arguably worse: active enforcement, moral police, custody sexual violence, hostile society. Dossier 3's courts decriminalising. I'd give dossier 4 ~0.10 and dossier 3 ~0.16. Let's say 4: 0.10, 3: 0.17.

Hmm, but rule 7: "sometimes lethal" is qualitative, no trans killings documented. Arrests on appearance are documented and recurring (2016, 2017, 2024 UPR). So high.

**Dossier 5:** Same-sex legal for centuries, hate crime/hate speech on SO criminalised and enforced (2010 conviction), but no gender-identity protections, no legal gender recognition, no Pride, ~10 people out, Catholic Church, anti-discrimination bill failed, reported discrimination rare, no torture/arbitrary detention reported (2023 official report), rank 45/49 region. Visitor-facing: no criminalisation of trans expression, no documented targeting, no border friction. Social climate: very low visibility, conservative, but discrimination "described as rare" and no abuses reported. So severity if outed: social friction/hostility (tier 3 at most, thin), no state threat. Score maybe 0.65-0.72. The absence of protections, low visibility, religious conservatism pull it down; but no documented exposure. Rule 13: no trans-specific criminal offence, no documented targeting, but no documented acceptance either (no third-gender tradition; Catholic conservatism). So below dossier 1's 0.76? Dossier 1 has documented acceptance (third-gender role) but a 14-year sodomy statute on books. Dossier 5 has no criminalisation at all but conservative society with rare discrimination. Hmm.

Rule 13 says: jurisdiction with (i) no trans criminal offence, (ii) no targeting, (iii) documented acceptance sits ABOVE those with similar machinery but no acceptance, and only moderately below acceptance+protections. Dossier 5 has (i) and (ii) but not (iii) — it has documented conservative/religious climate and low visibility, plus functioning rule of law with no abuses reported. Dossier 1 has (iii) but a latent statute.

Both thin-ish. Dossier 5's official report says no torture/arbitrary detention, and hate-crime enforcement works (conviction). Discrimination rare. I'd put dossier 5 around 0.70, dossier 1 around 0.74. Actually, is the latent 14-year statute a bigger deal than a conservative Catholic society? Rule 13: latent tangential statute + open questions + thin recourse = a step below acceptance-with-protections. Dossier 5's state: no criminalisation, functioning rule of law, but conservative society and no protections for gender identity. Everyday exposure: low-ish. Severity if outed: possible social hostility but documented discrimination rare, no state threat.

I'll go: Dossier 1 = 0.74, Dossier 5 = 0.70.

Dossier 2 = 0.89.

Let me reconsider Dossier 2 vs 1: clearly 2 higher.

Ordering: 4 (0.10) < 3 (0.17) < 5 (0.70) < 1 (0.74) < 2 (0.89).

Hmm. Dossier 4 documented 2024 UPR: arrests on clothing and appearance, 5-day detentions, bribes, trans women in male prisons with sexual violence, 2023 unit. That's current, pervasive, state-tolerated targeting (tier 2), plus hostile society (tier 3). I'll keep 4 = 0.10, 3 = 0.17. Reasonable.
